summary: MDM power/profile settings corrupt after provisioning - intermittent boot/power behavior on laptops
description:
Issue summary:
Multiple recently-provisioned laptops intermittently fail to resume correctly from shutdown or show incorrect Windows power plan and battery reporting. Symptoms occur after the automated MDM policy push that runs as part of the imaging pipeline (post-provision enrollment).

Impact:
- End users report machines that do not power on after closing the lid or rebooting (black screen, fans spinning).
- Devices show "Balanced (recommended)" in Settings but actually run on a high-performance kernel-level power policy (high drain).
- Affects new hires receiving fresh images and a subset of re-imaged deskside repairs. Estimated ~12 machines over the past 10 days in US-WEST.

Environment:
- MDM: Intune (company-managed tenant) with custom configuration profiles pushed via Enrollment Status Page + post-provision script.
- Imaging: SCCM/Autopilot hybrid flow triggering post-enrollment policy sync.
- Regions: us-west primary; single reports from eu-west for one repro.
- Firmware: mixed (some devices on 1.12 BIOS, others 1.10).

Steps to reproduce (observed):
1) Image device via our standard Autopilot + SCCM task sequence.
2) Device auto-enrolls into Intune and receives configuration profiles (security baseline, power/profile, telemetry).
3) Post-provision script (power-config-apply.sh converted to PowerShell) runs and triggers a policy sync.
4) Reboot or lid close/resume sometimes results in black screen or inconsistent power plan behavior.

Observed behavior:
- Black screen on initial resume; fans active; only hard reboot recovers.
- powercfg /list shows active plan GUID as the expected corporate GUID but power reporting (task manager, battery saver UI) indicates a different profile in effect.
- Event Viewer shows Kernel-Power ID 41 entries tied to abrupt wake/hard reboot.

Expected behavior:
- Normal resume from lid close/reboot, corporate power profile applied reliably, no Kernel-Power 41 events.

Attachments / Logs to check:
- SCCM task sequence logs for affected hosts (smsts.log) — attached to ticket for two hosts.
- Intune device sync history and policy assignment timestamps.
- powercfg outputs captured by end-users.
- BIOS versions and recent vendor release notes (Lenovo / Dell).

Notes:
- Seems correlated to machines that received the power/profile configuration within the first 10 minutes after Autopilot enrollment. Hypothesis: race between our post-provision script and the OS power service starting, causing duplicate or partially-applied registry keys.
investigation_notes:
Initial triage by desktop support (A. Morales) reproduced inconsistent resume on a Lenovo X1 with BIOS 1.10. Collected smsts logs and powercfg outputs. Engineering (SRE) ran live capture and observed Kernel-Power 41 after suspend. Reproduction appears intermittent and more likely when post-provision policy push occurs immediately after first boot.

Hypotheses considered:
- Race condition between Intune policy handler and our post-provision ps1 that writes power plan registry keys.
- BIOS firmware bug triggered by rapid policy changes during first boot (vendor notes show a suspend/resume fix in 1.12).
- Corruption of COM call to powercfg when executed from SYSTEM at early stage.

Actions taken so far:
- Rolled back the post-provision power assignment in the task sequence for the next 24h to let Intune apply profiles first (temporary gate).
- Collected additional smsts.log and Event Viewer exports and uploaded to artifact store.
- Opened vendor support case with Lenovo for X1 reproduction notes (case #LEN-2026-478).
- Created a small repro script that delays the power-profile application by 5 minutes after first login; initial manual runs did not reproduce the black-screen resume.

resolution: In Progress - Temporary workaround applied: removed immediate post-provision power profile step from task sequence and introduced scheduled task to apply corporate power plan 10 minutes after first login. Pending vendor firmware confirmation and longer-term fix to update imaging scripts to add delay/jitter. Follow-up: validate that repro rate drops to zero over next 72 hours, then consider pushing BIOS 1.12 to affected fleet if vendor confirms fix.
